title: Jeremiah (Part 1)
hook: Before Jeremiah ever spoke a word of judgment, God told him something staggering: "Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee" — a calling rooted not in Jeremiah's priestly pedigree from the quiet Levitical town of Anathoth, but in a relationship that predated his birth. Yet the oracles that follow are anything but gentle; God files what amounts to a covenant lawsuit against His own people, using the raw language of marital betrayal and even invoking a divorce law to describe how far Israel has wandered — a theological earthquake dressed in legal terms. Still, buried in the rubble of judgment is the Hebrew word *chesed*, that stubborn, binding, covenant love that refuses to let go even when every legal argument says it should. Jeremiah's own life becomes a living sermon — a priest's son, chosen before birth, sent to confront the very religious establishment that shaped him. There's something unexpectedly tender in watching a God of justice argue, plead, and ache for a people who've forgotten Him, and this week's study invites you to sit with that ache long enough to recognize your own story inside it.
